data.one_liner: Wrapper for WatchConnectivity on iOS and Wearable APIs on Android.
data.what_it_does: Provides a cross-platform wrapper to communicate between mobile devices and smartwatches (Apple Watch, Wear OS). Allows sending messages, updating application contexts, and listening for updates via streams.
use_when: You need to send messages or sync context data between a phone and an Apple Watch or Wear OS device.
You want to check if smartwatches are supported, paired, or reachable from your mobile app.
avoid_when: You are targeting platforms other than iOS and Android.
You need complex health workout integrations that require the removed startWatchApp functionality.
strengths: Supports both iOS WatchConnectivity and Android Wearable APIs in a unified API.
Provides stream-based listening for incoming messages and context updates.
weaknesses: Android platform limitations mean it cannot natively verify if a watch is paired or reachable, relying instead on app installations and node connections.
Android and watch apps must share the same package name and be signed with the same key.
data.setup_notes: On Android, the watch and phone apps must have the same package name and be signed with the same key.
